paras: The lynching of Monroe Wood was the reported killing of a Black man by a mob near Newville, Henry County, Alabama, in early August 1920. Wood was accused of insulting a white woman, and the only account, a secondhand report carried by the Montgomery Advertiser, said he was caught and shot to death.

According to a report that reached Dothan on Tuesday, August 10, Wood, described as "a negro," was lynched near Newville "for insulting a white woman one day last week." The wording leaves unclear whether "last week" dates the alleged insult or the killing itself. Wood was "said to have been caught north of Newville and shot to death by a mob"; the report gave no names of the mob's members and no number.
No report of an inquest, arrest, grand jury inquiry or official response was found in the coverage.

The killing appeared in the Montgomery Advertiser of August 12 as a brief item headed "Negro Is Lynched." in its "Dothan Notes" column, dated August 11. It ran between a notice of a family reunion and an announcement of a memorial service for Confederate dead, and it stated the insult accusation as the reason for the lynching without comment or confirmation. No other white paper and no Black paper was found carrying the report.

reader.title: Lynching of Monroe Wood
bases: The only report says Wood was 'lynched' and 'shot to death by a mob' over an alleged insult to a white woman (A2).

A2 reports Wood was shot to death by a mob, with no lawful authority mentioned, for allegedly insulting a white woman, a racial-tradition pretext; the mob's size is not given and the report is a single secondhand item ('according to a report reaching Dothan').
Only the Montgomery Advertiser's Dothan correspondent reported the killing, and only as a report that had reached Dothan (A2); no other paper in either press was found carrying it.

accounts.label: Dothan correspondent (secondhand report)
accounts.gist: A report reaching Dothan on Tuesday said Wood had been lynched near Newville for insulting a white woman one day the week before, caught north of town and shot to death by a mob.

framing.detail: The Montgomery Advertiser ran the killing as a four-line item, 'Negro Is Lynched.', between a family reunion notice and a Confederate memorial service, stating the insult accusation as the reason without comment.

record_check.dossier: About the first week of August 1920 ('one day last week' in an Aug. 11 dispatch); the report reached Dothan Aug. 10. The sentence is ambiguous whether 'last week' dates the insult or the lynching.
Supported: 'caught north of Newville and shot to death by a mob'.

record_check.record: Monroe Wood ... reportedly lynched near Newville ... for insulting a white woman the previous week
record_check.dossier: Supported, but it rests on a single secondhand report; the item does not clearly say the insult (rather than the lynching) happened 'last week'.
Confirmed: one white-press item; no Black-press coverage found.

set_aside: Posse killing of Sills Spinks and Jester Jennings at Midland City near Dothan, July 29-30; a different episode.
Ozark, Ala., Aug. 25: aftermath of the Spinks/Jennings lynching; no mention of Wood or Newville.
Editorial paragraph: 'a white man was lynched in Alabama for making an insulting remark to a white woman'; no name or place, victim called white; cannot be tied to this episode.
